skill.name: wunderui-screen
skill.description: Guides React screen development with WunderUI components, responsive layouts, design tokens, and loading, empty, and error states.
skill.summary: Build WunderUI screens with component discovery, plan-aware guidance, state checks, and project validation.
skill.author: wunder-ui

security_audit.summary: All 62 static findings are false positives involving documentation, JavaScript syntax, expected project reads, or public metadata requests. A semantic finding identifies plan enforcement that defaults to Pro and permits imports with unknown licensing metadata. No evidence found of malicious prompt injection, credential collection, or data exfiltration.

remediation.issue: Missing or unreadable plan configuration silently selects Pro; Core receives the same unrestricted treatment.
remediation.suggestion: Require an explicit, validated plan when configuration is unavailable, and enforce the documented component and block entitlements for each plan.

remediation.issue: Free-plan import checks accept components with unknown tiers when design metadata is missing or incomplete.
remediation.suggestion: Fail validation when licensing metadata cannot be loaded or an imported component lacks a known tier; report the missing metadata clearly.

semantic_findings.title: Plan Restrictions Fail Open
semantic_findings.description: Missing plan configuration defaults to Pro, and Core is not restricted separately. Free checks accept unknown component tiers when design metadata is unavailable or incomplete.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code restricts only Free and rejects only known Pro tiers, despite instructions to determine the user plan first. This permits licensing violations.

content.value_statement: Generated screens often miss UI states, responsive layouts, and consistent design tokens. This skill guides WunderUI component selection, screen assembly, and validation within the selected plan.
actual_capabilities: Ranks matching WunderUI blocks and components using local keyword scoring and public registry metadata.
Filters component suggestions for the Free plan and lists free alternatives to paid components.
Guides screen assembly using component signatures, responsive layouts, and typed sample data.
Requires loading, empty, and error states with development controls for reviewing them.
Checks specified source files for hardcoded colors, motion values, deep imports, missing states, and known paid imports on Free.
Directs the assistant to run the project typecheck, build, and motion audit after implementing the screen.
limitations: Requires a React project using WunderUI; the bundled helper requires Node.js 20 or later.
Block discovery requires network access, and component lookup requires local design metadata or access to the configured metadata site.
The checker uses regular expressions and file-level state detection; it does not verify runtime behavior or every data region.
Plan enforcement defaults to Pro and accepts unknown component tiers; confirm entitlements manually until these checks are fixed.

use_cases.title: Build Product Dashboards
use_cases.description: Assemble a responsive dashboard with plan-appropriate metrics, data regions, actions, and reviewable loading, empty, and error states.

use_cases.title: Prototype Settings Screens
use_cases.description: Create a Free-plan settings screen using forms, feedback components, design tokens, and invented sample data.

use_cases.title: Review Screen Consistency
use_cases.description: Check existing screen files for token violations, deep imports, missing state indicators, and known paid components before project validation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Settings Screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a WunderUI profile settings screen on the Free plan. Use invented data, design tokens, and loading, empty, and error states.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: create a small screen with explicit plan selection.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Responsive Dashboard
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a sales dashboard on my WunderUI Pro plan. Find matching blocks, verify component props, and add responsive layouts and reviewable UI states.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: adapt a matching block for a dashboard.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt a Screen for Free
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt my analytics screen for WunderUI Free. Replace paid components with documented free alternatives, preserve UI states, and explain the lost functionality.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: revise a screen to match available components.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Validate a Screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [screen files] for my confirmed WunderUI plan. Verify component signatures, tokens, motion, and every data region. Run checks, typecheck, and build.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: combine source checks with manual state review and project validation.

output_examples.input: Build a profile settings screen on the Free plan.
output: Illustrative result: a settings screen using free form and feedback components.
Loading, empty, and error states are available through a development status control.
The completion report identifies changed files, selected components, defaults, and validation results.

output_examples.input: Create a Free-plan revenue overview without paid charts.
output: Illustrative result: metric cards, trend indicators, and progress bars replace chart regions.
Loading placeholders, an empty overview, and retryable errors remain available.
The report notes that paid charts and the full app shell require an appropriate paid plan.

best_practices: Confirm the plan explicitly and verify component entitlements before accepting suggestions or importing blocks.
Read real component signatures and use design tokens before implementing each screen region.
Review each UI state on mobile and desktop, then run source checks, typecheck, and build.
anti_patterns: Treating a successful regex check as proof of runtime correctness or license compliance.
Copying paid component designs by hand to bypass plan restrictions.
Using real personal data, guessed props, or hardcoded motion and color values in generated screens.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code in a React project that uses WunderUI.

faq.question: What does the bundled helper do?
faq.answer: It searches component and block metadata, then checks specified source files for WunderUI conventions. The assistant performs screen implementation.

faq.question: Can I use the Free plan?
faq.answer: Yes. Specify Free explicitly and use documented free alternatives. Verify entitlements manually because missing metadata can bypass the helper checks.

faq.question: Does it need network access?
faq.answer: Block search retrieves a public registry index. Component metadata is read locally when available, otherwise it is fetched from the configured site.

faq.question: Does it guarantee a working screen?
faq.answer: No. Its regex checks are limited. The workflow also calls for project typechecking, building, and manual review of responsive layouts and UI states.

faq.question: Does it upload project source or credentials?
faq.answer: No evidence found of source or credential uploads in the bundled helper. Network requests retrieve metadata, and source checks read explicitly selected files.
